definitions.explanation: A type of fish cake made from surimi (ground fish paste) that is shaped and deep-fried. A common ingredient in Japanese home cooking, appearing in oden, udon, and as a side dish.

examples.japanese: おでんに{揚|あ}げかまぼこを{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I put deep-fried fish cake in the oden.

examples.japanese: {揚|あ}げかまぼこをそのまま{食|た}べてもおいしい。
examples.english: Deep-fried fish cake is delicious even eaten as is.

examples.japanese: スーパーで{揚|あ}げかまぼこを{二|ふた}つ{買|か}って、うどんに{入|い}れて{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I bought two deep-fried fish cakes at the supermarket and put them in udon.

notes:
Composed of {揚|あ}げ (deep-fried) and かまぼこ ({蒲鉾|かまぼこ}, fish cake). The generic term for any deep-fried variety of fish cake.

REGIONAL NAMES:
Called by different names across Japan:
- さつま{揚|あ}げ: the most common name in eastern Japan (originally from Satsuma/Kagoshima)
- {天|てん}ぷら: in western Japan, especially Kansai and Kyushu (not to be confused with the battered {天|てん}ぷら dish)
- はんぺん: in some regions (though {半片|はんぺん} usually refers to a different, softer fish cake)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {揚|あ}げかまぼこを{焼|や}く: to grill/toast deep-fried fish cake
- おでんの{揚|あ}げかまぼこ: deep-fried fish cake in oden
- {手作|てづく}り{揚|あ}げかまぼこ: homemade deep-fried fish cake

SIMILAR WORDS:
- かまぼこ ({蒲鉾|かまぼこ}): fish cake — the general category; usually refers to the steamed variety served on a wooden board
- さつま{揚|あ}げ: fried fish cake — the same product under its Kanto/standard name
- ちくわ ({竹輪|ちくわ}): tube-shaped fish cake — a different shape, with a hollow center
- {練|ね}り{物|もの}: surimi products — the general term for all processed fish paste products
